issues.legal_issue: An owner deprived of possession of property through compulsory requisition is entitled to interest on unpaid compensation for the period of deprivation, absent a clear statutory intention to exclude that entitlement.
material_facts: The appeal was confined to whether interest was payable on compensation awarded by an arbitrator for requisition of premises.
The owner had been deprived of possession of the premises, and part of the compensation remained unpaid during the period of deprivation.
The premises were later de-requisitioned and returned to the owner, and the principal compensation was paid by 31 July 1987.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were entitled to interest on the unpaid balance of the compensation for the relevant period of deprivation. Interest was payable at 6% per annum from 7 March 1975 to 28 February 1985, and at 12% per annum from 8 August 1985 to 31 July 1987; the latter rate applied only for that period. Interest was calculated on the balance remaining unpaid from the respective dates, and the appeal was disposed of with costs.
issues.legal_principle: Upon a statutory compulsory taking of property, interest on the compensation is ordinarily payable from the date possession is taken because it substitutes for the owner's lost right to retain possession; the taking of possession gives rise to an implied obligation to pay interest. The entitlement is not excluded merely because a statute makes compensation provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 applicable, unless the statute clearly indicates a contrary intention. The Court relied on Satinder Singh v. Amrao Singh, [1961] 3 SCR 676 at 694; National Insurance Co. Ltd., Calcutta v. Life Insurance Corporation of India, [1963] Supp. 2 SCR 971 at 992; Hirachand Kothari v. State of Rajasthan, [1985] Supp. 1 SCR 644 at 655; and Inglewood Pulp and Paper Co. Ltd. v. New Brunswick Electric Power Commission, AIR 1928 PC 287.

rule.if: requisition_compensation_appeal and owner_deprived_of_possession and compensation_unpaid_during_deprivation and no_clear_statutory_exclusion

predicates.requisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding concerns an appeal about interest on compensation awarded for compulsory requisition of property.
predicates.owner_deprived_of_possession: The owner lost possession of the property through the compulsory taking.
predicates.compensation_unpaid_during_deprivation: Some of the compensation remained unpaid while the owner was deprived of possession.
predicates.no_clear_statutory_exclusion: The applicable law did not clearly express an intention to exclude interest for the period of deprivation.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns compensation for compulsory requisition, the owner was deprived of possession, compensation remained unpaid during that deprivation, and the applicable law did not clearly exclude interest, interest is payable on the unpaid compensation for the period of deprivation.
